items.title: Section: Feeling, Mind, and Phenomena Contemplated — All Four Foundations Complete

items.zh: 於奢摩他品者，謂若汝心於內略時，起無相、無分別、寂靜想行，及無作用、無思慕無躁動、離諸燒惱寂滅樂想行；於所緣境無亂受等四無色蘊，剎那剎那展轉別異，唯是新新而非故故，相續流轉。汝應於此如理思惟，發起勝解。如是名為於內受、心、法修循受、心、法觀。
items.en: As for the calm-abiding type: when your mind gathers inward, giving rise to the perceptions of marklessness, non-discrimination, and tranquility … the undistracted formless aggregates of feeling and the rest, moment by moment, differ one from the next — each ever new, never the old repeated, continuing on in succession … This is called cultivating contemplation of feeling, mind, and phenomena with respect to the inner.

items.zh: 於無散亂品者，謂汝於先取諸境界、緣諸境界墮不定地過去盡滅，及今失念心亂所生諸相、尋思、隨煩惱境增上受等四無色蘊，汝應於此如理作意：如是諸法，其性皆是誑幻所作，暫時而有，率爾現前，多諸過患，其性無常，不可保信。汝應如是發起勝解。如是名為於外受、心、法修循受、心、法觀。於毘鉢舍那品者，謂汝善取毘鉢舍那相已，住有相、有分別作意，於有分別、有相所緣增上內所生受等四無色蘊，如理作意，思惟此法剎那剎那展轉別異，唯是新新而非故故，相續流轉。如前所說發起勝解。如是名為於內外受、心、法修循受、心、法觀。如是汝由依不淨觀正修加行增上力故，於四念住當得趣入。
items.en: As for the non-distraction type: with respect to the marks, discursive thoughts, and secondary afflictions arising from a prior lapse of mindfulness … all such phenomena are, by nature, entirely the work of deception and illusion — temporary, arising abruptly, fraught with danger, impermanent by nature, and not to be trusted. You should generate vivid understanding in this way. This is called cultivating contemplation of feeling, mind, and phenomena with respect to the outer. As for the insight type: having skilfully grasped the mark for insight, abiding in engagement that is marked and discriminating … This is called cultivating contemplation of feeling, mind, and phenomena with respect to both inner and outer. Thus, through the empowering force of correctly cultivating the practice by way of contemplation of impurity, you shall enter into the four foundations of mindfulness.

items.zh: 又汝應於念住加行，時時修習勝奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。汝於如是四念住中，安住正念，隨依彼彼村邑聚落邊際而住。於心隨順、趣向、臨入所緣境界，汝應捨此所緣境相，入彼村邑聚落乞食。

items.title: Section: Progressing Beyond the Cushion — Safety and Vigilance on the Almsround

items.zh: 應當善避惡象、惡馬、惡牛、惡狗、惡蛇、惡獸、坑㵎濠塹、株杌、毒刺、泥水、糞穢，及應遠離諸惡威儀、穢坐臥具。汝應如是善護己身。若於如是諸境界相不應策發諸根，汝應於彼不作功用，善守諸根。若於如是諸境界相應當策發諸根，汝應於彼正作功用，善住正念，令諸煩惱不起現行。
items.en: "You should skilfully avoid vicious elephants, horses, cattle, dogs, snakes, and wild beasts; pits, ravines, moats, tree-stumps, thorns, mud, and filth; and should keep away from improper deportment and unclean seats or bedding. In this way you should skilfully guard your own body. Where the faculties should not be engaged with such objects, you should apply no effort towards them, skilfully guarding the faculties. Where the faculties should be engaged with such objects, you should rightly apply effort towards them, skilfully abiding in mindfulness, so that no affliction is allowed to manifest."

items.zh: 汝應如是善護己身、善守諸根、善住正念；於彼作意，善知其量受用飲食。
又汝應與在家出家說應量語、說應理語、說應時語、說正直語、說寂靜語。一切世間非法言論，皆當遠離。雖復宣說如法言論，不應諍競。何以故？若諸士夫補特伽羅住諍競語，互相難詰，其心便住多戲論中；多戲論故，其心掉舉；心掉舉故，心不寂靜；不寂靜故，便令其心遠三摩地。
items.en: "Further, with householders and renunciants alike, you should speak words that accord with the valid means of knowledge, and words that are reasoned, timely, upright, and tranquil. Every worldly discourse contrary to the Dharma should be entirely avoided. And even in speaking words in accord with the Dharma, you should not engage in contention. Why is this? Because if persons abide in contentious speech, disputing with one another, their minds come to dwell in much idle discourse; through much idle discourse, the mind becomes agitated; through an agitated mind, the mind loses tranquility; and through lost tranquility, the mind is driven far from samādhi."

items.zh: 如是行已，汝應速疾不捨所緣，結跏趺坐，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，如所取相，由恒常作及畢竟作，修瑜伽行。

items.title: Section: The Vow of Unlimited Practice, and the Simile of Kindling Fire — Contemplation of Impurity's Teaching Closes

items.zh: 猶如世間鑽火方便，起無間加行及殷重加行，汝應如是恒常修作、畢竟修作。又汝應起如是願心：假使一切贍部洲人，盡贍部洲曾經壽量，今皆總集在我一身，我亦盡此無量壽命，決定於斷瑜伽作意勝奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，精勤修習，時無暫捨。
items.en: "Just as, in the world, the method of kindling fire by friction requires uninterrupted and earnest effort, so too should you cultivate constantly and to completion. Further, you should give rise to this resolve: 'Suppose the combined lifespans of every person who has ever lived on this continent were all gathered together into this one body of mine — even with such a boundless lifespan, I would resolutely, diligently cultivate the superior mental engagement of calm-abiding and insight that severs affliction, without abandoning it for even a moment.'"

items.zh: 由正了知如是所修瑜伽加行，有大勝果、大勝利故。何況如是少分壽量、少時存活，雖極遠去不過百年，委悉算計但須臾頃。如是汝應隨所教誨，恒常修作、畢竟修作。若為此義受習於斷，汝於此義必當獲得。汝當最初證得下劣身心輕安，心一境性，後當證得世出世間廣大圓滿。
items.en: "Knowing correctly that such cultivated yogic practice bears great and excellent fruit, great and excellent benefit — how much more so, then, given how brief a lifespan you actually have, living at most a hundred years, which, carefully reckoned, amounts to no more than a single muhūrta. Thus you should, according to this instruction, cultivate constantly and to completion. You shall first attain a modest degree of bodily-mental pliancy and one-pointedness of mind, and later attain the vast, complete fulfilment of both the mundane and supramundane paths."

items.zh: 初修業者始修業時，善達瑜伽諸瑜伽師，依不淨觀如是教誨，名正教誨；如是修行，名正修行。如說貪行，是不淨觀之所調伏；如是瞋行，是慈愍觀之所調伏；乃至最後尋思行，是阿那波那念之所調伏；如其所應，皆當了知。其中差別餘趣入門，我當顯示。

blocks.text: The other three foundations of mindfulness, then practical guidance for life outside meditation, and a resolve against laziness. A short passage (0462c17) is untranslated.

When the mind gathers inward, "the formless aggregates of feeling and the rest, moment by moment, differ one from the next, each ever new, never the old repeated". Venerable Miào Jìng: every moment is new. And the marks, thoughts, and afflictions that arise through lapses "are entirely the work of deception and illusion, temporary, arising abruptly, fraught with danger".
"Avoid vicious elephants, horses, cattle, dogs, snakes; pits, ravines, thorns, mud, and filth." Guard the senses: "where the faculties should not engage, apply no effort towards them".

"Speak words that are measured, reasoned, timely, upright, and tranquil." "Even in speaking words in accord with the Dharma, do not engage in contention." Master Cháng Bǎi: "through much idle talk the mind becomes agitated".

"Just as kindling fire by friction requires uninterrupted effort, so should you cultivate constantly." And a resolve: "Suppose the lifespans of everyone who has ever lived on this continent were gathered into this one body of mine: even with such a boundless lifespan, I would cultivate calm and insight without abandoning it for a moment." "How much more, then, given how brief your life actually is: at most a hundred years, which, reckoned carefully, is no more than a moment."
The advice on speech is worth keeping for any discussion, including our own conversations about this text: speak reasonably, at the right time, calmly, and without needing to win.

quiz.q: "The undistracted four formless aggregates of feeling and the rest" — the note says "three formless aggregates." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — four, without the great elements; Cháng Bǎi: form is grasped by perception, mind by names
quiz.why: "The undistracted formless aggregates of feeling and the rest, moment by moment, differ — each ever new, never the old." Venerable Miào Jìng: feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — these four aggregates lack the great elements; they are the four formless aggregates. Master Cháng Bǎi: form can be grasped by perceptual seeing and hearing; mental phenomena must be grasped through names. The note's "three" is wrong.

quiz.q: "Each ever new, never the old" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: every arising instant is new, never lasting to a second — so new, never old
quiz.why: "Moment by moment, differ one from the next — each ever new, never the old repeated." Venerable Miào Jìng: every arising moment is new; it doesn't remain to a second moment, so all is new, not old.

quiz.q: On the almsround, "skilfully avoid vicious elephants, horses, cattle, dogs." What does Venerable Miào Jìng warn?
options: protect yourself — don't say "I practise, I'm not afraid"
quiz.why: "You should skilfully avoid vicious elephants, horses, cattle, dogs, snakes, and wild beasts; pits, ravines, moats …" Venerable Miào Jìng: don't be harmed by them — protect yourself. Don't say, "I practise, I'm not afraid!"

quiz.q: "應量語" is rendered "measured words." How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng: not contradicting direct perception — "there's a dragon here" violates it; Cháng Bǎi: truthful speech, not claiming absorption one lacks
quiz.why: "Speak words that are measured, reasoned, timely, upright, and tranquil." Venerable Miào Jìng: saying "there's a dragon here" violates direct perception, since no one can see it. Master Cháng Bǎi: 應量語 is truthful speech — don't claim absorption you haven't attained. The English "measured" suggests moderation; the lectures take it as accord with valid cognition.

quiz.q: "Even speaking in accord with Dharma, don't contend." What does Master Cháng Bǎi relay from Miào Jìng?
options: one quarrel and samādhi is gone — destroyed by anger
quiz.why: "Even in speaking words in accord with the Dharma, you should not engage in contention." Master Cháng Bǎi: Venerable Miào Jìng said, quarrel with someone and come back — your samādhi is gone, destroyed by anger.

quiz.q: "Just as kindling fire by friction" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi apply the simile?
options: practice calm and insight without break until the fire of wisdom appears
quiz.why: "Just as, in the world, the method of kindling fire by friction requires uninterrupted and earnest effort, so too should you cultivate constantly and to completion." Master Cháng Bǎi: practice calm and insight constantly without interruption, to completion — until the fire of wisdom comes forth.

quiz.q: "Carefully reckoned, a mere 須臾" — the English says "a fleeting moment." How do the masters read 須臾?
options: both: 48 minutes — after distractions, meals, and sleep, that's all the real practice time in a day
quiz.why: "Living at most a hundred years, which, carefully reckoned, amounts to no more than a fleeting moment." Venerable Miào Jìng: 須臾 is forty-eight minutes — subtract distractions, meals, and sleep from a lifetime, and how much time is left? Master Cháng Bǎi: real practice time in a day is no more than a 須臾 of 48 minutes. The English is more general.
